critical_code_review_comments: P0-1 fix is architecturally correct: `opened = (pos_id > 0)` (line 1762) makes position resolution the ONLY path to reporting an open trade — no more masquerading of order ticket as position id.

The JR_ACCEPTED redispatch handler (lines 1557-1574) is the essential safety half of P0-1: on redispatch we re-resolve the position from history/comment scan, and if still unresolved we re-emit 'accepted_unresolved' — no OrderSend under any branch. Confirmed by inspection.

Backend accepted_unresolved handler (bridge_routes.py 1098-1120) correctly (a) returns 'already_open'/'already_closed' when replayed after resolution (line 1104), (b) never persists mt5_ticket=0 (falsy guard on line 1138 applies), (c) stores order_ticket/deal_ticket for later reconciliation.

OrderFilledVolume (mq5:535) is the correct P0-2 fix — sums DEAL_VOLUME over deals where DEAL_ORDER == our order ticket, so under netting the trade's fill is attributed by DEALS not by the aggregated position volume. Position volume is reported separately as position_volume (line 1739 → SendOpenReport signature).

P0-3 half-step tolerance (`filled + half_step < req.volume`, line 1743) is the right way to compare against the broker's volume step — avoids false partial-fill flags from floating-point rounding when broker fills exactly the requested volume.

Nit (unchanged from iter69): PartialFillAdopted audit event is written (verified live), but the corresponding closing/reconciliation flow still doesn't cross-reference this event by event_id when computing realised risk. Consider surfacing it in /api/bot/execution-health or a dedicated risk-audit endpoint so the desk can filter partially-filled trades quickly.
